# Table: `jl-table`

Rows of records under column headings, with sorting, selection, rows that open on their details, formats and a sticky header.

- Class `JlTable`, a organism: `import { JlTable } from '@syware/jlib';`
- On the site: https://bioleyl.github.io/jlib/components/table

A table for records: users, invoices, deployments. Describe the columns once (what each shows, its
format, whether it sorts) and give the rows as plain objects; the table formats numbers and dates for the reader's
language, draws badges and code, and right-aligns numbers.

A press on a sortable heading sorts the rows ascending, then descending, then back to their order, and emits sort.
Numbers sort by value, dates by time, text in the language's order; empty values stay at the end. selectable adds a
checkbox to each row and one in the header that selects them all (a dash when only some are), and emits selection
with the keys of the selected rows, read from row-key.

expandable lets rows open: a press on a row, or on its chevron, shows its detail under it, and the row stays as it
is. single keeps one row open, opening another closes it; multiple opens any number. detail draws what an open row
shows, from its row; expanded holds the keys of the open rows, and each opening and closing emits toggle.

The header stays on top while the rows scroll within max-height, and the table scrolls sideways on narrow screens.
For a cell that is more than a value (a person with an avatar, a link, a menu), give the column a renderer.

## Use

```ts
import { JlTable } from '@syware/jlib';
```

```tsx
<JlTable
  columns={[{"key":"name","label":"Name","sortable":true},{"key":"status","label":"Status","format":"badge","tones":{"Active":"ok","Invited":"info"}},{"key":"projects","label":"Projects","format":"number","sortable":true}]}
  expandable="single"
  rows={[{"id":1,"name":"Ada Lovelace","status":"Active","projects":12,"email":"ada@acme.dev","joined":"2023-02-14"},{"id":2,"name":"Ben Okafor","status":"Invited","projects":4,"email":"ben@acme.dev","joined":"2024-06-03"},{"id":3,"name":"Chen Wei","status":"Active","projects":27,"email":"chen@acme.dev","joined":"2024-11-21"}]}
  selectable
/>
```

```html
<jl-table
  columns='[{"key":"name","label":"Name","sortable":true},{"key":"status","label":"Status","format":"badge","tones":{"Active":"ok","Invited":"info"}},{"key":"projects","label":"Projects","format":"number","sortable":true}]'
  expandable="single"
  rows='[{"id":1,"name":"Ada Lovelace","status":"Active","projects":12,"email":"ada@acme.dev","joined":"2023-02-14"},{"id":2,"name":"Ben Okafor","status":"Invited","projects":4,"email":"ben@acme.dev","joined":"2024-06-03"},{"id":3,"name":"Chen Wei","status":"Active","projects":27,"email":"chen@acme.dev","joined":"2024-11-21"}]'
  selectable
></jl-table>
```

## Properties

Inputs: a JSX prop sets one, code calls `.set(value)` and `.get()`, HTML writes the attribute (lists and objects as JSON).

- `columns` (attribute `columns`): `TableColumn<Row>[]`, default `[]`. The columns: key (the field shown), label, and optionally align, sortable, width, format (text, number, date, datetime, badge, code), tones (a badge tone per value), description (a field shown as a quieter line under the value) and wrap (long text breaks over lines instead of widening the table). Typed by the rows, key and description are fields of a row.
- `rows` (attribute `rows`): `Row[]`, default `[]`. The rows, as plain objects of the page's own type: JlTable<Order> takes orders. Untyped, any object.
- `rowKey` (attribute `row-key`): `keyof Row | 'id'`, default `'id'`. The field that tells rows apart, for the selection.
- `sortKey` (attribute `sort-key`): `keyof Row | ''`, default `''`. The column the rows are sorted by.
- `sortDirection` (attribute `sort-direction`): `'none' | 'asc' | 'desc'`, default `'none'`. The order of that column.
- `selectable` (attribute `selectable`): `boolean`, default `false`. Adds a checkbox to each row, and one that selects them all.
- `selected` (attribute `selected`): `Array<string | number>`, default `[]`. The keys of the selected rows.
- `expandable` (attribute `expandable`): `'none' | 'single' | 'multiple'`, default `'none'`. Rows open on a press, on the row or its chevron, to show their detail under them: single one at a time (opening a row closes the other), multiple any number.
- `expanded` (attribute `expanded`): `Array<string | number>`, default `[]`. The keys of the open rows. When they open one at a time, the last one is open.
- `detail` (property only): `((row: Row) => Node) | null`, default `null`. Draws what an open row shows under it, from its row: (order) => Node, the order typed as the table is. Drawn when the row opens.
- `marked` (attribute `marked`): `Array<string | number>`, default `[]`. The keys of rows to draw attention to, such as a search's matches: a bar at their start and a shade. A mark, not a selection: nothing acts on them.
- `dense` (attribute `dense`): `boolean`, default `false`. Shorter rows.
- `striped` (attribute `striped`): `boolean`, default `false`. Shades every other row.
- `maxHeight` (attribute `max-height`): `string`, default `''`. A height past which the rows scroll under the header: 320px, 50vh; a number is pixels.
- `emptyText` (attribute `empty-text`): `string`, default `''`. What the table says when it has no rows. Empty: jlib's own text, in the language shown.
- `loading` (attribute `loading`): `boolean`, default `false`. Shows placeholder rows while the data loads.
- `label` (attribute `label`): `string`, default `''`. The name of the table for screen readers.
- `renderers` (property only): `{ [key in keyof Row]?: (row: Row) => Node }`, default `{}`. Draws the cells of some columns by code, by column key: (row) => Node, the row typed as the table is. For a table that does not say its type of row, cellOf<Row>((row) => …) writes one for the page's own type.

## Events

In JSX, the `on…` prop, its handler given the detail; in code, `events.register(name, (detail) => …)`. They do not bubble.

- `sort` (`onSort` in JSX), detail `{ key: keyof Row; direction: 'asc' | 'desc' | 'none' }`: A heading was pressed: the column and its new order.
- `selection` (`onSelection` in JSX), detail `Array<string | number>`: The selection changed: the keys of the selected rows.
- `toggle` (`onToggle` in JSX), detail `{ key: string | number; open: boolean }`: A row opened or closed: its key and whether it is open now. When rows open one at a time, opening a row emits the close of the other first.

## Methods

- `toggle(key: string | number, open: boolean): void`: Opens or closes a row, as a press on it would, and emits toggle. When rows open one at a time, opening one closes the other.

## Styling

- `base` (part, `::part(base)`): The scrolling frame around the table.

## Typing

Typed by its rows, JlTable<Order> takes rows of the page's own type, an interface included. Its columns (TableColumn<Order>) name fields of an order, and so do rowKey and sortKey: the editor completes them and refuses a misspelt one. Its renderers, its detail and its sort event read an order. In JSX, <JlTable rows={orders} /> reads the type from the rows. A column that is not a field, such as one of actions a renderer draws, is named: JlTable<Order, 'actions'>. Rows and columns written as JSON in HTML are not checked.

```ts
import type { JlTable, TableColumn } from '@syware/jlib';

type Order = { id: number; number: string; customer: string; total: number; note?: string };

const COLUMNS: TableColumn<Order>[] = [
  { description: 'note', key: 'customer', label: 'Customer', sortable: true },
  { format: 'number', key: 'total', label: 'Total', sortable: true },
];

export function showOrders(root: HTMLElement, orders: Order[]): void {
  const table = root.querySelector<JlTable<Order>>('jl-table.orders');
  if (table === null) {
    return;
  }
  table.columns.set(COLUMNS);
  table.rows.set(orders); // an interface's rows too
  table.sortKey.set('total');
  // @ts-expect-error: an order has no `totl`
  table.sortKey.set('totl');
  table.renderers.set({ total: (order) => document.createTextNode(order.total.toFixed(2)) });
  table.detail = (order) => noteOf(order); // order: Order, not Record<string, unknown>
}
```

```tsx
import { Jadis } from '@jadis/core';
import { JlTable } from '@syware/jlib';

import type { TableColumn } from '@syware/jlib';

type Order = { id: number; number: string; customer: string; total: number; note?: string };

const COLUMNS: TableColumn<Order>[] = [
  { description: 'note', key: 'customer', label: 'Customer', sortable: true },
  { format: 'number', key: 'total', label: 'Total', sortable: true },
];

export class OrdersView extends Jadis {
  static readonly selector = 'orders-view';

  private readonly _refs = this.useRefs((ref) => ({ orders: ref<JlTable<Order>>('.orders') }));

  templateHtml(): Node {
    // The props are checked against an order: sortKey="totl" does not compile.
    return <JlTable<Order> class="orders" columns={COLUMNS} sortKey="total" expandable="single" />;
  }

  async onConnect(): Promise<void> {
    const table = this._refs.orders;
    table.detail = (order) => noteOf(order);
    table.rows.set(await loadOrders());
  }
}

OrdersView.register();
```

## Examples

HTML as the site renders it, with its layout classes (`row`, `stack`, `narrow`, `muted`), which are not jlib's: a view writes the same components by class in JSX. A script's `root` is the example's element.

### Workspace members

Sorting on every column, a badge for the status, and a selection the toolbar acts on.

```html
<div class="stack">
  <div class="row">
    <span class="muted selection-count">No user selected</span>
    <jl-button class="remove-selected" size="sm" variant="danger" icon="trash" label="Remove" disabled></jl-button>
  </div>
  <jl-table class="users" label="Workspace members" selectable sort-key="name" sort-direction="asc"
    columns='[{"key":"name","label":"Name","sortable":true},{"key":"email","label":"Email","sortable":true},{"key":"role","label":"Role","sortable":true},{"format":"badge","key":"status","label":"Status","sortable":true,"tones":{"Active":"ok","Invited":"info","Suspended":"danger"}},{"format":"number","key":"projects","label":"Projects","sortable":true},{"format":"date","key":"joined","label":"Joined","sortable":true}]'></jl-table>
</div>
```

```js
type Member = { id: number; name: string; email: string; role: string; status: string; projects: number; joined: string };

const table = root.querySelector<JlTable<Member>>('jl-table.users');
const count = root.querySelector('.selection-count');
const remove = root.querySelector<JlButton>('.remove-selected');
table.rows.set([
  { id: 1, name: 'Ada Lovelace', email: 'ada@acme.dev', role: 'Owner', status: 'Active', projects: 12, joined: '2023-02-14' },
  // …
]);
table.events.register('selection', (keys) => {
  count.textContent = keys.length === 0 ? 'No user selected' : `${keys.length} selected`;
  remove.disabled.set(keys.length === 0);
});
remove.events.register('press', () => {
  const selected = new Set(table.selected.get());
  table.rows.set(table.rows.get().filter((member) => !selected.has(member.id)));
  table.selected.set([]);
});
```

### Custom cells

A renderer draws the cells of a column by code; here a name with its email under it. The cells live in the table's shadow root, out of reach of the page's styles: style what a renderer draws inline.

```html
<jl-table class="people" columns='[{"key":"name","label":"Person","sortable":true},{"key":"role","label":"Role"},{"key":"projects","label":"Projects","format":"number"}]'></jl-table>
```

```js
const table = root.querySelector<JlTable<Member>>('jl-table.people');
table.renderers.set({
  name: (member) => {
    const cell = document.createElement('div');
    cell.innerHTML = '<strong></strong><div class="email" style="color: var(--jl-muted); font-size: 13px"></div>';
    cell.querySelector('strong').textContent = member.name;
    cell.querySelector('.email').textContent = member.email;
    return cell;
  },
});
table.rows.set(members.slice(0, 4));
```

### Row details

A press on a row, or on its chevron, opens it: its detail comes under it, the row staying as it is. One row at a time opens by default here; the other choice lets any number stay open. The detail lives in the table's shadow root: draw it with jl-* components, or style it inline.

```html
<div class="stack">
  <jl-segmented class="expansion" label="Rows that open" value="single"
    options='[{"value":"single","label":"One at a time"},{"value":"multiple","label":"Any number"}]'></jl-segmented>
  <jl-table class="orders" expandable="single" label="Orders" columns='[{"format":"code","key":"number","label":"Order","width":100},{"key":"customer","label":"Customer","sortable":true},{"format":"badge","key":"status","label":"Status","tones":{"Delivered":"ok","Shipped":"info","Waiting":"warn"}},{"format":"number","key":"total","label":"Total","sortable":true},{"format":"date","key":"placed","label":"Placed","sortable":true}]'></jl-table>
</div>
```

```js
type Order = { id: number; number: string; customer: string; address: string; items: string; note?: string; … };

const table = root.querySelector<JlTable<Order>>('jl-table.orders');
table.detail = (order) => {
  const facts = new JlFacts();
  facts.items.set([
    { label: 'Deliver to', value: order.address },
    { label: 'Items', value: order.items },
    { label: 'Note', value: order.note ?? null },
  ]);
  return facts;
};
table.rows.set(orders);
root.querySelector<JlSegmented>('.expansion').events.register('change', (value) =>
  table.expandable.set(oneOf(TABLE_EXPANSIONS, 'single')(value))
);
```

Dense and striped, the header held on top while the rows scroll within 260 pixels.

```html
<jl-table class="deploys" dense striped max-height="260" label="Deployments"
  columns='[{"format":"code","key":"commit","label":"Commit","width":110},{"key":"branch","label":"Branch","sortable":true},{"format":"badge","key":"state","label":"State","tones":{"Failed":"danger","Live":"ok","Queued":"neutral"}},{"format":"number","key":"duration","label":"Seconds","sortable":true},{"format":"date","key":"at","label":"Date","sortable":true}]'></jl-table>
```

```js
root.querySelector('jl-table.deploys').rows.set(deployments);
```

### Loading and empty

Placeholder rows while the data loads, and a sentence when there is none.

```html
<div class="stack">
  <jl-table loading columns='[{"key":"name","label":"Name"},{"key":"email","label":"Email"},{"key":"amount","label":"Amount","format":"number"}]'></jl-table>
  <jl-table empty-text="No invoices yet" columns='[{"key":"number","label":"Invoice"},{"key":"customer","label":"Customer"},{"key":"total","label":"Total","format":"number"}]'></jl-table>
</div>
```

### Formats

Each format, written in HTML: rows can be JSON in the attribute too.

```html
<jl-table row-key="sku"
  columns='[{"key":"sku","label":"SKU","format":"code"},{"key":"product","label":"Product"},{"key":"stock","label":"Stock","format":"badge","tones":{"In stock":"ok","Low":"warn","Out":"danger"}},{"key":"price","label":"Price","format":"number","sortable":true},{"key":"updated","label":"Updated","format":"date","sortable":true}]'
  rows='[{"sku":"KB-104","product":"Keyboard","stock":"In stock","price":89.5,"updated":"2025-04-02"},{"sku":"MS-220","product":"Mouse","stock":"Low","price":39,"updated":"2025-05-18"},{"sku":"HD-310","product":"Headset","stock":"Out","price":1249,"updated":"2025-01-27"}]'></jl-table>
```

### Long text

Cells keep to one line and the table scrolls sideways; a column with wrap breaks its long text over lines instead.

```html
<jl-table row-key="field"
  columns='[{"key":"field","label":"Field","width":"28%"},{"key":"value","label":"Value","wrap":true}]'
  rows='[{"field":"title","value":"Minutes of the town council, 1952 to 1957"},{"field":"description","value":"The council\u2019s minutes, bound by year, with the indexes of the decisions and the letters received, as the clerk kept them."},{"field":"storedAt","value":"https://archive.example.com/objects/rr_1622818982000013/i_2/content/minutes-1952-1957.pdf"}]'></jl-table>
```

### Marked rows

Marked rows, here the properties a search for “title” matches, stand out among the others.

```html
<jl-table row-key="name" marked='["title","additionalTitle"]'
  columns='[{"key":"name","label":"Property","format":"code"},{"key":"kind","label":"Kind"},{"key":"description","label":"Description","wrap":true}]'
  rows='[{"name":"abstract","kind":"string","description":"Abstract summarizing the resource."},{"name":"additionalTitle","kind":"string","description":"Another title of the resource."},{"name":"extent","kind":"string","description":"How much there is."},{"name":"title","kind":"string","description":"The name of the resource."}]'></jl-table>
```
